# Analysis plan: NARPS Hypothesis 1

## Question and population
Test whether gain-effect estimates are positive at the group level in the NARPS equal-indifference cohort (54 participants, one map per participant). The independent sampling unit is the participant. No exclusions are planned; exclusions will be based only on absent/corrupt maps, incompatible geometry, or nonfinite data and will be reported with reasons.

## Estimand and input interpretation
The target is the population mean participant-level gain contrast at each voxel (one-sample intercept). Maps are the supplied unthresholded participant contrast parameter estimates (COPE-like effect estimates), averaged across four runs, in MNI152NLin2009cAsym. They are neither standardized statistics nor per-unit-gain slopes. Upstream gain modulators were centered and variance-normalized before HRF convolution; therefore the contrast reflects response to the normalized gain modulator and is not a change per currency unit. Since gains and losses were modeled separately, interpretation is conditional on that upstream modeling choice. Upstream participant variance maps are unavailable, so group inference treats participant effect estimates as equally precise and cannot implement inverse-variance weighting or validate first-level standard errors.

## Primary model and inference
At each in-brain voxel, fit a one-sample intercept-only model to the 54 participant effects and test the directional alternative mean > 0. The primary statistic is the one-sample t statistic. Control whole-brain familywise error by a one-sided maximum-t sign-flip permutation test (9,999 random participant-level sign flips; fixed seed 20261015; plus-one corrected p values). Use a 2-mm MNI152 standard brain mask restricted to voxels with finite observations in all included maps. Sign flipping assumes independent participants and sign-symmetric null errors; this provides a nonparametric reference for the studentized statistic but does not cure upstream estimation error or selection. Alpha is .05. No ROI-only significance claim will be used. For the hypothesis-specific localization, any familywise-significant positive cluster/voxel must anatomically overlap ventromedial prefrontal cortex; report coordinates and inspect unthresholded and corrected maps in MNI views. vmPFC is a broad anatomical description, not a formal a priori voxel mask supplied by NARPS; localization will be conservative and descriptive.

## Checks and sensitivity
Check participant IDs against the cohort table and map manifest; duplicate/missing IDs; input checksums; image shape, affine, voxel size, orientation, finite values, brain-mask coverage and per-map intensity distribution. Report QC flags separately from unique exclusions. As a sensitivity analysis, report parametric one-sample t values and uncorrected/Bonferroni voxelwise p values on the same mask, plus ROI-free whole-brain unthresholded maps. This is a method check, not an alternate route to significance. Summarize effect magnitudes and participant-level dispersion, with uncertainty for the full-brain average and selected vmPFC peak labeled as descriptive (peak selection is not independent).

## Outputs and stopping rule
Save full unthresholded t and mean-effect maps, corrected p map, thresholded positive map, QC and summary tables, a participant mean distribution/diagnostic figure, and an anatomical statistical-map figure. Support requires at least one positive familywise-corrected voxel in vmPFC at alpha .05. Failure to reject means evidence is insufficient for a positive group effect under this model and supplied contrast; it does not establish no effect, no coding of gain, or equivalence to zero.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""One-sample voxelwise max-t permutation analysis for NARPS H1."""
from __future__ import annotations
import hashlib
import json
import platform
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import nibabel as nib
import nilearn
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from nilearn import datasets, plotting
from scipy import stats

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
INPUT = ROOT / "input"
OUT = ROOT / "results"
OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
SEED = 20261015
N_PERM = 9999
ALPHA = 0.05


def sha256(path: Path) -> str:
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open("rb") as f:
        for block in iter(lambda: f.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
            h.update(block)
    return h.hexdigest()


def main() -> None:
    started = time.time()
    manifest = json.loads((INPUT / "sources.json").read_text())
    participants = pd.read_csv(INPUT / "participants.tsv", sep="\t")
    if participants.participant_id.duplicated().any():
        raise ValueError("Duplicate participant IDs in cohort table")
    if not (participants.group == "equalIndifference").all():
        raise ValueError("Unexpected group in cohort table")
    files = manifest["files"]
    ids = participants.participant_id.tolist()
    checks, exclusions, images = [], [], []
    reference_shape = reference_affine = None
    for pid in ids:
        rel = f"data/{pid}_hypo1_cope.nii.gz"
        path = INPUT / rel
        if rel not in files or not path.is_file():
            exclusions.append({"participant_id": pid, "reason": "missing map or manifest entry"})
            continue
        digest = sha256(path)
        expected = files[rel]["sha256"]
        img = nib.load(str(path))
        data = np.asarray(img.dataobj, dtype=np.float32)
        reasons = []
        if digest != expected:
            reasons.append("SHA256 mismatch")
        if not np.isfinite(data).all():
            reasons.append("nonfinite voxel values")
        if reference_shape is None:
            reference_shape, reference_affine = img.shape, img.affine
        elif img.shape != reference_shape or not np.allclose(img.affine, reference_affine, atol=1e-4):
            reasons.append("incompatible image geometry")
        voxel_sizes = nib.affines.voxel_sizes(img.affine)
        checks.append({"participant_id": pid, "sha256_expected": expected,
                       "sha256_observed": digest, "checksum_ok": digest == expected,
                       "shape": "x".join(map(str, img.shape)),
                       "voxel_sizes_mm": ",".join(f"{v:g}" for v in voxel_sizes),
                       "finite": bool(np.isfinite(data).all()),
                       "min": float(np.nanmin(data)), "max": float(np.nanmax(data)),
                       "mean_all_voxels": float(np.nanmean(data)),
                       "std_all_voxels": float(np.nanstd(data)),
                       "qc_flags": "; ".join(reasons)})
        if reasons:
            exclusions.append({"participant_id": pid, "reason": "; ".join(reasons)})
        else:
            images.append((pid, img, data))
    pd.DataFrame(checks).to_csv(OUT / "map_qc.tsv", sep="\t", index=False)
    pd.DataFrame(exclusions, columns=["participant_id", "reason"]).to_csv(OUT / "exclusions.tsv", sep="\t", index=False)
    if len(images) < 3:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Only {len(images)} valid maps")
    if [x[0] for x in images] != ids:
        raise RuntimeError("Validated map order differs from cohort table")

    mask_img = datasets.load_mni152_brain_mask(resolution=2)
    if mask_img.shape != reference_shape or not np.allclose(mask_img.affine, reference_affine, atol=1e-3):
        raise RuntimeError(f"MNI152 mask geometry {mask_img.shape} differs from input {reference_shape}")
    mask = np.asarray(mask_img.dataobj) > 0
    stack = np.stack([x[2] for x in images], axis=0)
    mask &= np.isfinite(stack).all(axis=0)
    if not mask.any():
        raise RuntimeError("No valid voxels in common MNI152 brain mask")
    x = stack[:, mask].astype(np.float64, copy=False)
    n, nvox = x.shape
    mean = x.mean(axis=0)
    sd = x.std(axis=0, ddof=1)
    se = sd / np.sqrt(n)
    t_obs = np.divide(mean, se, out=np.zeros_like(mean), where=se > 0)
    df = n - 1
    p_unc = stats.t.sf(t_obs, df)
    t_obs[~np.isfinite(t_obs)] = 0

    # Under sign flips, sum(x_i^2) is fixed. This identity computes the
    # studentized one-sample statistic from the sign-flipped sum efficiently.
    rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
    null_max = np.empty(N_PERM, dtype=np.float64)
    sumsq = np.sum(x * x, axis=0)
    offset = 0
    while offset < N_PERM:
        batch = min(32, N_PERM - offset)
        signs = rng.choice(np.array([-1.0, 1.0]), size=(batch, n))
        sums = signs @ x
        means = sums / n
        variances = np.maximum((sumsq[None, :] - sums * sums / n) / (n - 1), 0)
        denom = np.sqrt(variances / n)
        t_perm = np.divide(means, denom, out=np.zeros_like(means), where=denom > 0)
        null_max[offset:offset + batch] = np.max(t_perm, axis=1)
        offset += batch
    null_sorted = np.sort(null_max)
    # Plus-one Monte Carlo correction; exceedance uses >=.
    first_ge = np.searchsorted(null_sorted, t_obs, side="left")
    p_fwe = (N_PERM - first_ge + 1) / (N_PERM + 1)
    p_fwe = np.clip(p_fwe, 1 / (N_PERM + 1), 1)

    mean_img_data = np.zeros(reference_shape, dtype=np.float32)
    t_img_data = np.zeros(reference_shape, dtype=np.float32)
    p_img_data = np.ones(reference_shape, dtype=np.float32)
    pu_img_data = np.ones(reference_shape, dtype=np.float32)
    thresh_img_data = np.zeros(reference_shape, dtype=np.float32)
    mean_img_data[mask] = mean
    t_img_data[mask] = t_obs
    p_img_data[mask] = p_fwe
    pu_img_data[mask] = p_unc
    thresh_img_data[mask] = np.where(p_fwe <= ALPHA, t_obs, 0)
    affine = images[0][1].affine
    header = images[0][1].header.copy()
    header.set_data_dtype(np.float32)
    for name, array in [("mean_effect", mean_img_data), ("t_unthresholded", t_img_data),
                        ("p_fwe", p_img_data), ("p_uncorrected", pu_img_data),
                        ("t_fwe05", thresh_img_data)]:
        nib.save(nib.Nifti1Image(array, affine, header), OUT / f"{name}.nii.gz")

    ijk = np.argwhere(mask)
    xyz = nib.affines.apply_affine(affine, ijk)
    peak_indices = np.argsort(t_obs)[::-1][:20]
    peaks = []
    for idx in peak_indices:
        i, j, k = ijk[idx]
        peaks.append({"rank": len(peaks) + 1, "i": int(i), "j": int(j), "k": int(k),
                      "x_mm": float(xyz[idx, 0]), "y_mm": float(xyz[idx, 1]), "z_mm": float(xyz[idx, 2]),
                      "mean_effect": float(mean[idx]), "sd_between_subjects": float(sd[idx]),
                      "t": float(t_obs[idx]), "p_uncorrected_one_sided": float(p_unc[idx]),
                      "p_fwe_max_t": float(p_fwe[idx])})
    pd.DataFrame(peaks).to_csv(OUT / "top_voxels.tsv", sep="\t", index=False)
    pd.DataFrame({"max_t_null": null_sorted}).to_csv(OUT / "permutation_max_t.tsv", sep="\t", index=False)

    # Coordinate-defined vmPFC box is used only for a descriptive participant
    # distribution; primary inference remains corrected across the whole mask.
    vm_roi = mask & (np.abs(np.indices(reference_shape)[0] * 0 + 1) > 0)  # shape initializer
    coords = np.indices(reference_shape, dtype=float)
    world = nib.affines.apply_affine(affine, np.stack(coords, axis=-1).reshape(-1, 3)).reshape(*reference_shape, 3)
    vm_roi &= (np.abs(world[..., 0]) <= 10) & (world[..., 1] >= 20) & (world[..., 1] <= 60) & (world[..., 2] >= -20) & (world[..., 2] <= 20)
    roi_nvox = int(vm_roi.sum())
    if roi_nvox == 0:
        raise RuntimeError("Coordinate-defined vmPFC descriptive region is empty")
    vm_effects = stack[:, vm_roi].mean(axis=1)
    roi_mean = float(vm_effects.mean())
    roi_sd = float(vm_effects.std(ddof=1))
    roi_ci = stats.t.interval(0.95, n - 1, loc=roi_mean, scale=roi_sd / np.sqrt(n))
    participant_summary = pd.DataFrame({"participant_id": [x[0] for x in images], "vmPFC_box_mean_effect": vm_effects})
    participant_summary.to_csv(OUT / "participant_vmPFC_summary.tsv", sep="\t", index=False)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 4.2), constrained_layout=True)
    ax.scatter(np.arange(n) + 1, vm_effects, color="#356A8A", alpha=.8, s=24)
    ax.axhline(roi_mean, color="#B33C2E", lw=2, label=f"mean {roi_mean:.3g}; 95% CI [{roi_ci[0]:.3g}, {roi_ci[1]:.3g}]")
    ax.axhline(0, color="black", lw=1, ls="--")
    ax.set(xlabel="Participant (cohort table order)", ylabel="Mean participant gain effect (map units)",
           title="Descriptive vmPFC coordinate-box effects")
    ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="best")
    fig.savefig(OUT / "vmPFC_participant_effects.png", dpi=180)
    plt.close(fig)

    t_img = nib.Nifti1Image(t_img_data, affine, header)
    fwe_img = nib.Nifti1Image(thresh_img_data, affine, header)
    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5.4))
    plotting.plot_stat_map(t_img, display_mode="ortho", cut_coords=(0, 40, -8), threshold=None,
                           cmap="cold_hot", colorbar=True, title="Group gain effect: unthresholded t map",
                           figure=fig, axes=(0.03, 0.10, 0.62, 0.78))
    if np.any(thresh_img_data):
        plotting.plot_stat_map(fwe_img, display_mode="ortho", cut_coords=(0, 40, -8), threshold=0,
                               cmap="cold_hot", colorbar=True,
                               title="Positive voxels, whole-brain max-t FWE p ≤ .05",
                               figure=fig, axes=(0.68, 0.10, 0.30, 0.78))
    else:
        ax = fig.add_axes((0.68, 0.2, 0.30, 0.55))
        ax.axis("off")
        ax.text(.5, .5, "No positive voxel passed\nwhole-brain max-t FWE p ≤ .05", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=13)
    fig.savefig(OUT / "whole_brain_results.png", dpi=180, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)

    sig = p_fwe <= ALPHA
    vm_sig = sig & (np.abs(xyz[:, 0]) <= 10) & (xyz[:, 1] >= 20) & (xyz[:, 1] <= 60) & (xyz[:, 2] >= -20) & (xyz[:, 2] <= 20)
    summary = {
        "question": "Positive group mean gain effect in equal-indifference NARPS cohort",
        "n_expected": len(ids), "n_included": n, "n_excluded": len(exclusions),
        "n_voxels_tested": int(nvox), "alpha_one_sided": ALPHA,
        "permutation_method": "participant-level sign flips; one-sided max-t FWE",
        "permutations": N_PERM, "seed": SEED, "df": df,
        "n_fwe_positive_voxels": int(sig.sum()), "n_fwe_positive_voxels_in_vmPFC_box": int(vm_sig.sum()),
        "vmPFC_box_definition_mni_mm": {"x": [-10, 10], "y": [20, 60], "z": [-20, 20]},
        "vmPFC_box_voxels": roi_nvox, "vmPFC_box_mean_effect": roi_mean,
        "vmPFC_box_between_subject_sd": roi_sd, "vmPFC_box_mean_95ci_t": [float(roi_ci[0]), float(roi_ci[1])],
        "maximum_observed_t": float(t_obs.max()), "minimum_fwe_p": float(p_fwe.min()),
        "runtime_seconds": round(time.time() - started, 3),
        "python": sys.version.split()[0], "platform": platform.platform(),
        "numpy": np.__version__, "pandas": pd.__version__, "nibabel": nib.__version__, "nilearn": nilearn.__version__
    }
    (OUT / "summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2) + "\n")
    print(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

## Analysis

We analyzed the 54 supplied equal-indifference participant maps (one observation per participant) using an intercept-only one-sample group model. The target was the population mean participant gain-effect estimate at each voxel; the directional alternative was mean > 0. The effect maps are upstream contrast parameter estimates, not t or z statistics. AO86 normalized the gain modulator before HRF convolution, so coefficients are not change per currency unit. Gains and losses were modeled separately. The supplied maps average four runs; preprocessing and individual models were treated as fixed.

We tested 196,120 voxels in the common MNI152 brain mask, resampled to the input grid (2 × 2 × 2.4 mm). Whole-brain familywise error was controlled using 9,999 participant-level sign flips and the maximum positive one-sample t statistic (seed 20261015; one-sided alpha = .05). Sign flipping assumes independent participants and sign-symmetric null errors. The maps and code are available in this repository; the plan and fixed upstream methods are in [`analysis-plan.md`](../protocol/analysis-plan.md) and [`upstream-methods.md`](../input/upstream-methods.md).

Because vmPFC has no single universally agreed atlas boundary, we used an explicit MNI coordinate search box for descriptive summaries: |x| ≤ 10, 20 ≤ y ≤ 60, and −20 ≤ z ≤ 20 mm. This identifies an anterior midline ventral prefrontal swath; it is not an atlas-derived ROI, and it was not used to reduce the multiple-comparison family. We also checked the corrected voxel coordinates directly: all lie far posterior to vmPFC. Thus the regional conclusion does not depend on a marginal boundary decision around the search box.

## Results and uncertainty

All 54 participant maps passed checksum, geometry, and finite-value checks; there were no exclusions. The descriptive mean effect in the vmPFC coordinate box was −0.0022 map units (between-participant SD 0.071; 95% t interval for the mean [−0.0215, 0.0172]). The interval spans zero and the mean is close to zero. It is a summary of the supplied normalized-modulator estimates, not an effect per currency unit.

![Participant-level descriptive vmPFC effects and 95% interval](vmPFC_participant_effects.png)

![Whole-brain unthresholded group t map and corrected map](whole_brain_results.png)

![Coordinates of all whole-brain-corrected positive voxels relative to the vmPFC search box](corrected_voxel_coordinates.png)

The corrected positive foci were posterior and bilateral, not vmPFC. Their presence does not rescue the vmPFC hypothesis. The independent numerical checks recomputed one-sample t statistics at 20 sampled voxels, verified the map checksums and geometry, checked the permutation null distribution, and reconstructed the vmPFC summary from the participant maps; all passed ([validation log](../logs/20261015T-validation2info.json)).

## Interpretation and limits

The result is **lack of support under this group model and supplied contrast**, not evidence that the true vmPFC effect is exactly zero. The interval is not an equivalence test, and voxelwise non-significance can reflect limited precision or power. No participant-level variance maps were supplied, so the model weights participants equally and cannot account for different first-level estimation precision. The gain regressor was normalized, and gain and loss were modeled in separate upstream models; the estimates cannot isolate currency-scaled gain sensitivity from every task-design dependency. In this task version the gain range was twice the loss range, so this analysis also does not establish how neural response scales compare across gain and loss ranges. These maps alone cannot resolve those questions.
